newsitem.title: USA: Pittsburgh may appeal decision to allow KKK rally.
newsitem.headline: Pittsburgh may appeal decision to allow KKK rally.

text.p: City officials said Friday they may appeal a federal judge's decision to allow the Ku Klux Klan to hold a rally here next month, after the city had denied the white supremacist group a permit.

"We'll know whether there will be an appeal by late Friday or early Monday," said Jacob Brody, spokesman for Mayor Tom Murphy. He said Murphy was disappointed with Thursday's ruling by U.S. District Judge Alan N. Bloch.
KKK members were not available for comment.
The Klan earlier this month applied for a permit to hold a rally in Pittsburgh on April 5, asking the city to supply police protection and an electrical hookup for a sound system.
Murphy denied the permit, citing public safety concerns, which prompted the KKK to file a civil suit against the city.

At a hearing held Thursday, Bloch ruled the group is entitled to free speech and said it could hold a "peaceful, nonviolent" rally on April 5 in downtown Pittsburgh. He said by denying the original permit, city officials exceeded their power to regulate the use of public streets and buildings.

At the time he denied the permit, Murphy said he did so because the KKK, besides holding a downtown rally, wanted to demonstrate in Homewood, a predominantly black neighbourhood. He said that demonstration would likely cause an outbreak of violence and he denied the permit for safety reasons.
